overview: The Ptolemies ruled Egypt from Alexandria, combining Macedonian kingship with Egyptian royal traditions. Ptolemy I adopted the royal title in 305 BCE; the dynasty ended with Roman takeover in 30 BCE.

items.text: Alexandria combined a planned street grid with palaces, libraries, temples and a harbor marked by the Pharos lighthouse.
Greek circulated alongside Egyptian Demotic. Immigration and settlement brought varied communities into Egypt, including the Fayum.
Royal support sustained Egyptian temples and priestly scholarship. The cult of Serapis connected Egyptian divine traditions with Alexandrian religious life.
Workshops produced colorful faience and glass inlays. Linen, farming and exchange connected Egypt with Mediterranean and longer-distance networks.
Artists adapted Egyptian and Greek forms to different audiences. Some portraits combined Greek hairstyles with Egyptian poses, while funerary works often retained traditional forms.

sources.title: Marsha Hill, Met, Egypt in the Ptolemaic Period
